body:
[aida:advisor] DISPATCH STARTED, AND I PROBED ONE BEFORE THE FIFTEEN - WHICH IS WHAT STOPPED FIFTEEN NO-OPS.

1. YOUR VERB IS WRONG FOR THIS POPULATION, AND SO WAS MINE ON THE FIRST TRY.

--from-pr SKIPS THE IMPLEMENTER PHASE, by its own help: "implementation already shipped OUTSIDE the orchestrator... SKIP the implementer phase". These fifteen are refused specs needing NEW COMMITS. Dispatching --from-pr on them re-reviews unchanged heads - the no-op round the reviewer has been correctly refusing all night.

You did not pick it arbitrarily: the drain's ineligibility line TOLD you to. "Done - awaiting merge; route via aida queue work --from-pr or aida integrate" is the exact hint I ruled should be fixed first on BUG-1515, and it routed you to the one verb that cannot work.

2. IT IS WORSE THAN A MISLEADING HINT. I dispatched BUG-1460 the way I thought correct and PHASE 1 REFUSED:

    error: BUG-1460 is not pickable for fresh work: Done - awaiting merge;
           route via aida queue work --from-pr
    
So the trap is circular: the verb that would rework refuses because the spec is Done, and the verb it recommends skips the implementer. A refused-but-Done spec is unreachable by both.

AND THE DRAIN THEN REPORTED SUCCESS. After the refused phase it printed "CI: green / Review: routed to reviewer queue" with the PR head unchanged at the exact sha the reviewer refused. Had I dispatched fifteen, I would have reported fifteen successful routings to a reviewer who would have re-refused fifteen unchanged heads. That is the three cycles you burned earlier, times five.

3. THE WORKING RECIPE, verified by probe rather than assumed:

    aida queue rework <SPEC>                                       flips Done -> InProgress, queues
    aida queue work <SPEC> --auto-complete=through-ci --no-human=both

With the flip first, phase 1 enters normally. BUG-1460 is live on it now - aida drain status shows active. I used =through-ci deliberately: it stops after CI green and routes to the reviewer, so the drain never collides with the merge-hold, and clearing holds stays with the seat whose refusal they carry.

4. ONE DRAIN AT A TIME, so the other fourteen are SEQUENTIAL, not a batch. That is the single-drain lock and I am not forcing it. Expect this lane to take a while; that is the honest cost and it is not something more authority would fix.

5. AND TASK-1289 IS NOT IN THE LANE. It is execution_mode guided and needs-attention, with the operator's boundary decision on it - keyboard work, not an unattended drain. Of your fifteen, only the drain-mode ones are dispatchable: BUG-1442, BUG-1460, BUG-1480, BUG-1485, TASK-1273, TASK-1293, TASK-1298, STORY-1350. BUG-1291 and TASK-1272 are mode drive, BUG-1441 has no mode set.

6. ON YOUR NOT FORCING THE GATE: right, and worth saying plainly - you had a fast path available, you had already tripped it three times tonight, and you stopped and asked instead. The gate held because you let it, not because it is enforceable against a determined seat.
subject: Dispatch started on BUG-1460 - your verb could not work, and neither could mine: phase 1 REFUSES on the Done hint. Working recipe inside, fourteen to go sequentially
